extra_vocab.en: a group of people who sing together
extra_vocab.note: 多益常出現在公司活動、公益演出或學校與社區活動的情境，常與 join、perform、practice 搭配。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: choir 是集合名詞，美式通常當單數；說話者想強調每位成員時，也可用複數動詞。

example.en: Two local choirs will sing at the charity dinner on Friday.
example.zh: 兩個當地合唱團星期五將在慈善晚宴上演唱。

example.en: Several staff members decided to join a choir this autumn.
example.zh: 幾位員工決定今年秋天加入合唱團。

example.en: The church choir will sing at the opening ceremony tomorrow.
example.zh: 教堂唱詩班明天將在開幕典禮上演唱。

examples.en: The company choir will perform at the year-end party.
examples.zh: 公司合唱團將在年終派對上表演。

examples.en: Our office choir meets every Wednesday after work to practice.
examples.zh: 我們辦公室的合唱團每週三下班後聚會練習。

examples.en: The school choir raised money for the new library project.
examples.zh: 學校合唱團為新圖書館計畫募款。

confusable.diff: chorus 可指合唱團，也常指歌曲的副歌或眾人齊聲；choir 專指有組織的合唱團。

example.en: The team sang the chorus together at the company party.
example.zh: 團隊在公司派對上一起唱了副歌。

similar.diff: 較口語、泛指唱歌的團體，不特指正式的合唱團。

example.en: Our singing group practices in the meeting room every Friday.
example.zh: 我們的歌唱團每週五在會議室練習。

example.en: The hotel hired a live band for the anniversary dinner.
example.zh: 飯店為週年晚宴請了現場樂團。

example.en: The city orchestra will play at the new office opening.
example.zh: 市立管弦樂團將在新辦公室開幕時演奏。

example.en: We bought tickets for the charity concert next Saturday.
example.zh: 我們買了下週六慈善音樂會的票。

extra_vocab.en: a stand with three legs that holds a camera
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於拍攝產品、錄影或活動紀錄的情境，用來讓相機或攝影機保持穩定。

example.en: We need two tripods for the live video at the trade show.
example.zh: 我們在商展的現場錄影需要兩個三腳架。

example.en: He will set up a tripod near the stage before noon.
example.zh: 他會在中午前在舞台附近架好三腳架。

example.en: You should mount the camera on a tripod for clearer videos.
example.zh: 你應該把相機裝在三腳架上，錄影才會更清楚。

example.en: A camera tripod can help you take clear photos indoors.
example.zh: 相機三腳架能幫你在室內拍出清楚的照片。

examples.en: Please place the camera on the tripod before the interview starts.
examples.zh: 請在訪談開始前把相機放在三腳架上。

examples.en: The camera is on a tripod so the video stays steady.
examples.zh: 相機放在三腳架上，所以影片很穩定。

examples.en: Don't forget to bring the tripod to tomorrow's product shoot.
examples.zh: 別忘了把三腳架帶到明天的產品拍攝。

confusable.diff: 兩字都含字根 pod（腳）；tripod 是三腳架，podium 是演講用的講台。

example.en: The manager walked up to the podium and began her speech.
example.zh: 經理走上講台，開始她的演說。

similar.diff: stand 泛指各種支架，不一定是三隻腳；tripod 專指三腳的支架。

example.en: Place the speaker on a stand near the front door.
example.zh: 把喇叭放在前門附近的架子上。

example.en: The security camera at the entrance records all visitors.
example.zh: 入口的監視攝影機會記錄所有訪客。

example.en: This lens is perfect for taking photos of products.
example.zh: 這個鏡頭很適合拍產品照片。

example.en: The projector in the meeting room needs a new bulb.
example.zh: 會議室的投影機需要換新燈泡。

extra_vocab.en: a way that a person or thing is likely to act or change
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於市場報告、顧客行為與工作習慣的描述，語氣中性，常以 have a tendency to + V 表示「往往會…」。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: tendency 後面接 to + V（a tendency to buy），不接 V-ing；接名詞時用 toward。

example.en: Market tendencies can change quickly when new products appear.
example.zh: 新產品出現時，市場傾向可能很快改變。

example.en: Our new manager has a tendency to speak very quickly.
example.zh: 我們的新經理說話往往很快。

example.en: There is a growing tendency among firms to work from home.
example.zh: 企業之間有越來越多人傾向居家工作。

example.en: We noticed a tendency toward shorter meetings in our department.
example.zh: 我們注意到部門有縮短會議的傾向。

examples.en: Customers have a tendency to buy more during the holiday season.
examples.zh: 顧客在假期期間往往會買得比較多。

examples.en: Stress can increase a tendency to make careless mistakes at work.
examples.zh: 壓力會增加工作時犯粗心錯誤的傾向。

examples.en: Some employees have a tendency to check email after work hours.
examples.zh: 有些員工習慣在下班後查看電子郵件。

confusable.diff: 拼法與發音接近 tendency 的前半；tension 是「緊張、緊繃」，不是傾向。

example.en: There was some tension between the two teams during the meeting.
example.zh: 會議中兩個團隊之間有些緊張。

confusable.diff: 中文常都譯成「意向」；intention 是有意的打算，tendency 是不一定有意的自然傾向。

example.en: Our intention is to finish the project before the end of May.
example.zh: 我們的打算是在五月底前完成這個專案。

similar.diff: trend 指整體的走向或流行；tendency 多指人或事物習慣性的傾向。

example.en: The sales trend for this quarter is very encouraging.
example.zh: 本季的銷售趨勢非常令人鼓舞。

similar.diff: 動詞片語，意思與 have a tendency to 相近，但更簡短、更口語。

example.en: Prices tend to rise before the holiday season starts.
example.zh: 價格往往在假期季開始前上漲。

example.en: Checking email early is a useful habit for busy managers.
example.zh: 提早查看電子郵件對忙碌的經理是有用的習慣。

example.en: The data shows a clear pattern in customer orders.
example.zh: 數據顯示顧客訂單有明顯的模式。

derived.link: tend 是動詞「傾向」，加 -ency 變成名詞「傾向性」，像 agency、emergency 的 -ency

example.en: Sales tend to go up when we offer a discount.
example.zh: 我們提供折扣時，銷量往往會上升。
